system_description.narrative_title: AI, Bond Stress, and Strategic Rivalries Reshape the Global Order
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is in dynamic flux as a tech-driven rivalry between major powers (notably the US and China) plays out alongside mounting financial stress from a deep bond-market rout and sharply higher borrowing costs. Regional conflicts — from Iran and the Gulf to Russia-Ukraine — are amplifying energy and supply-chain shocks, while the rapid AI build-out both accelerates economic concentration and raises systemic governance and financial-risk questions. These interacting processes create feedback loops that raise the probability of policy errors, market dislocations, and ad-hoc diplomatic bargains.
system_description.scope: State actors and major power interactions (US, China, EU, Russia, Middle Eastern actors), global financial markets (bonds, FX, credit), energy and commodity supply chains, technology and AI industrial ecosystems, multinational corporations and major trade flows, regional conflict theatres and international institutions.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-security system (the integrated international political-economy and technological order)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system (sovereign debt, bond markets, monetary policy)
Energy & commodity networks (oil, diesel, shipping through Hormuz/Red Sea)
Advanced technology & AI industrial ecosystem (data centres, chips, agents)
Regional security theatres (Middle East, Eastern Europe, Indo-Pacific)

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting diplomatic influence, trade terms and regional security (notably over Taiwan), reshaping great‑power interaction and norms of engagement.

variables.name: AI build‑out and systemic tech risks
variables.description: A rapid, capital‑intensive global build‑out of AI models and data‑centre infrastructure by Big Tech and competitors is shifting economic and technological power while creating new financial, regulatory and systemic risks.

variables.name: Iran‑Gulf military and maritime confrontation
variables.description: Iran, U.S. partners, Saudi‑aligned forces and Houthi proxies are engaged in escalating military and maritime clashes that threaten Gulf shipping, oil flows and regional security.

variables.name: Russia’s war and European security scramble
variables.description: Russia’s campaign in Ukraine and stepped‑up strikes are driving a broader European security crisis that is forcing NATO and EU states to deepen intelligence, defence cooperation and contingency planning.

variables.name: Global bond market repricing and monetary shift
variables.description: A sustained surge in long‑term yields led by U.S. Treasuries is recalibrating central‑bank expectations, tightening financing conditions, raising borrowing costs worldwide and altering capital flows.
